translations.literal: Hu Gui was a native of Yanzhou.
At first he served Zhu Jin as central-army commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He first served Zhu Jin as a central-army commandant.

translations.zh: 兗州平，署為宣武軍都虞候。
translations.literal: When Yanzhou was pacified, he was appointed Xuanwu Army chief adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: After Yanzhou fell he was made chief adjutant of the Xuanwu Army.

translations.zh: 佐葛從周伐鎮、定，從張存敬收晉、絳，皆有功，署為河中都虞候，榷鹽務。
translations.literal: He aided Ge Congzhou in attacking Zhen and Ding, followed Zhang Cunjing in taking Jin and Jiang—all with merit—and was appointed chief adjutant of Hezhong and put in charge of the salt monopoly.
translations.idiomatic: He helped Ge Congzhou against Zhen and Ding and Zhang Cunjing against Jin and Jiang, winning merit each time; he was then made chief adjutant of Hezhong and put in charge of the salt monopoly.

translations.zh: 天復中，太祖迎駕至岐下，以規權知洽州。
translations.literal: In Tianfu, when the Founder welcomed the imperial carriage to Qixia, he made Gui acting prefect of Qiazhou.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianfu, when the Founder welcomed the emperor to Qixia, he made Gui acting prefect of Qiazhou.

translations.zh: 昭宗還長安，詔授皇城使。
translations.literal: When Zhaozong returned to Chang'an, an edict appointed him imperial-city commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaozong returned to Chang'an, an edict made him imperial-city commissioner.

translations.literal: When the court moved east, he was made imperial-camp commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the court moved east, he was made imperial-camp commissioner.

translations.literal: When the carriage reached Luoyang, he was appointed commissioner of the inner gardens and estates.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor reached Luoyang, he was made commissioner of the inner gardens and estates.

translations.zh: 天祐三年，佐李周彝討相州，獨當州之一面，頗以功聞，軍還，權知耀州事。
translations.literal: In Tianyou 3 he aided Li Zhouyi against Xiangzhou, alone holding one face of the prefecture, and won considerable fame; when the army returned he was acting prefect of Yaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianyou 3 he aided Li Zhouyi at Xiangzhou, holding one sector of the siege alone and winning fame; after the campaign he acted as prefect of Yaozhou.

translations.zh: 明年，討滄州，為諸軍壕寨使。
translations.literal: The next year, campaigning against Cangzhou, he was trench-and-camp commissioner for the armies.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the campaign against Cangzhou, he served as trench-and-camp commissioner for the combined armies.

translations.zh: 太祖受禪，除右羽林統軍，尋佐劉鄩統兵收潼關，擒劉知浣獻之，乃以為右龍虎統軍兼侍衛指揮使。
translations.literal: When the Founder received the mandate, Gui was made Right Feathered Forest commander; soon he aided Liu Yan in leading troops to recover Tong Pass, captured Liu Zhihuan and presented him, and was then made Right Dragon-Tiger commander and also commander of the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the Liang founding he was made Right Feathered Forest commander; he soon helped Liu Yan recover Tong Pass, captured Liu Zhihuan and presented him, and was then made Right Dragon-Tiger commander and commander of the palace guard.

translations.zh: 乾化元年，詔修洛河堤堰，軍士因之斬伐百姓園林太甚，河南尹張宗奭奏之，規得罪，賜死。
translations.literal: In Qianhua 1 an edict ordered repair of the Luo River dikes; soldiers used this to cut down commoners' gardens and groves far too much; Henan governor Zhang Zongshi memorialized it; Gui was found guilty and ordered to die.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianhua 1 an edict ordered repairs on the Luo River dikes; soldiers used the work to strip commoners' gardens and groves, and Henan governor Zhang Zongshi reported it; Gui was condemned and put to death.
